input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: § 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment on us expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — squarely in the playbook's walk-away territory (multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or exit) and well short of the fallback (12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up instead of penalty). It also directly conflicts with § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment, and with the Order Form–based fee structure in § 7.1. We therefore replaced § 2.1 with the preferred position (pay only for Services used or ordered), offering the 12-month reducible/true-up fallback in the comment.

proposal.summary: Remove the three-year take-or-pay minimum; Customer pays only for Services used or ordered.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment: our playbook does not accept multi-year minimum purchase commitments with no reduction or termination right, and the clause also contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment. If a commitment is commercially necessary, we can discuss one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and settled by a true-up rather than a penalty.

ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: Customer will pay only for Services used or ordered during the applicable term. Customer has no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, or shortfall obligation.
